detail.abstract: Researchers have started using LLM agents in place of human subjects in behavioural and politicalscience experiments, often as a cheaper substitute for laboratory pools. The substitution does not hold up in strategic settings: humans and LLMs reliably make different choices, and neither fine-tuning on human response data nor persona conditioning has closed the gap. The behavioural-economics literature has, since Simon's introduction of bounded rationality, modelled human strategic behaviour as a classical baseline plus an additive correction term δ. The framework proposed here reads δ as the mathematical signature of bounded computation: the gap between what an unboundedly-rational agent would compute and what a computationally bounded agent actually produces. For canonical games whose solutions are present in standard training corpora, LLMs retrieve and recombine corpus material, bypassing the bound that produces δ in humans. The framing extends to reasoning-distilled models through cognitive-hierarchy theory: their accessible level-k strategic reasoning is bounded by compute budget and context length rather than by the cognitive constraints that bound humans, and the δ they produce, if any, carries different structural signatures. Four operational tests (conditional dependence, distributional asymmetry, path-dependence under repetition, and paraphrase-robustness) are proposed to discriminate human-shaped δ from LLM-shaped δ. A moderator prediction is that |δ| scales with peer-signal individuation in the decision environment, with a quantitative bound of Cohen's d ≥ 0.5 between named-opponent and aggregate-opponent settings.

title: Genetic K-Means for Missing-Value Imputation
affiliations: Universidade Federal Fluminense, Universidade Federal Fluminense, Universidade Federal Fluminense and Universidade Federal Fluminense

detail.title: Genetic K-Means for Missing-Value Imputation
detail.abstract: This study examines whether missing-value imputation in K-means clustering can be reformulated as an optimization problem guided by clustering quality. To address this question, the paper proposes Genetic K-means, a hybrid framework in which a Genetic Algorithm searches the space of candidate imputations and evaluates each solution through the Silhouette score obtained after applying K-means. The method was tested on three benchmark datasets from the UCI repository after inducing artificial missingness under an MCAR mechanism at 5\%, 10\%, and 20\%. Its performance was compared with min-max value replacements, mean filling, and k-Nearest Neighbors imputation using both Silhouette score and RMSE. Across all three datasets and all missingness levels, Genetic K-means achieved the highest Silhouette values, including 0.7154, 0.6744, and 0.5631 for Wholesale Customers, 0.2044, 0.2853, and 0.2433 for Travel Reviews, and 0.2675, 0.2894, and 0.3122 for Cervical Cancer Behavior Risk. In contrast, it did not consistently attain the lowest RMSE. These findings indicate that reconstruction accuracy and clustering adequacy are not equivalent objectives. The originality of the study lies in introducing an imputation framework for unsupervised learning in which evolutionary search is explicitly aligned with structure-preserving clustering performance, thereby extending missing-data treatment beyond conventional reconstruction-oriented logic.

title: Digital Dualism: Platform Capitalism, Informality, and Structural Transformation in the Global South
affiliations: Imperial College London

detail.title: Digital Dualism: Platform Capitalism, Informality, and Structural Transformation in the Global South
detail.abstract: Rapid digitalization has transformed markets across the Global South, yet its developmental consequences remain deeply uneven. In many late-industrializing economies, the expansion of digital platforms has occurred alongside persistent informality, weak productivity growth, and increasing concentration of economic power. This paper develops the concept of digital dualism to explain this configuration. Bringing structural transformation theory into dialogue with the political economy of platform capitalism, the paper argues that digitalization may only reorganize rather than overcome dualistic economic structures. Network effects, data advantages, and global platform governance concentrate value capture within a small number of firms, while limited labour absorption and uneven productivity diffusion leave large segments of the workforce in low-productivity informal activities. These dynamics are illustrated through cross-country stylized evidence and comparative analysis of India and Brazil. The paper contributes to debates on digital capitalism and development by showing how digital expansion can reinforce existing hierarchies while generating new forms of concentration and dependency in late-industrializing economies.

title: Implementation and evaluation of an operational seasonal precipitation forecasting system for Cuba using PyCPT
affiliations: University of Havana, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Implementation and evaluation of an operational seasonal precipitation forecasting system for Cuba using PyCPT
detail.abstract: Seasonal precipitation forecasts are a key component of climate services in Cuba, where rainfall variability affects agriculture, water management, drought monitoring, public health, and disaster risk reduction. This study presents the implementation and evaluation of an operational forecasting framework based on the Python Climate Predictability Tool (PyCPT), using CFSv2 predictors and the national Solvaz gridded dataset as predictand. CCA and PCR statistical approaches were compared, evaluating five predictors from lead 0 to lead 6 months: Atlantic sea surface temperature (ASST), outgoing longwave radiation (OLR), temperature at 850 hPa (T850), zonal wind at 200 hPa (200UA), and zonal wind at 30 hPa (30UA). Verification combines deterministic and probabilistic metrics with climatological diagnostics to assess reproduction of the known seasonal behavior of Cuban rainfall. Both methods reproduce the observed annual cycle, including the dry-season minimum and the rapid onset of the rainy season. Forecast skill is strongly season-dependent: MAM, JJA, and SON show the most useful skill, while DJF remains challenging because precipitation is episodic and driven by extratropical disturbances. The skillful predictors are physically consistent with dominant rainfall mechanisms: OLR, T850, and 200UA contribute substantially during the rainy season, reflecting tropical convection, lower-tropospheric thermodynamics, and upper-level circulation; ASST contributes in selected months; and 30UA has weaker relevance. An operational example for 2021 illustrates the system capacity to reproduce broad seasonal structures while revealing positive biases during wet-season months. Overall, PyCPT provides a reproducible and physically interpretable framework for seasonal precipitation forecasting in Cuba and a basis for strengthening Caribbean climate services.

title: A Multi-Objective Machine Learning Approach for Crash Severity Prediction under Class Imbalance in Less-Regulated Driving Environments
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Multi-Objective Machine Learning Approach for Crash Severity Prediction under Class Imbalance in Less-Regulated Driving Environments
detail.abstract: Predicting crash injury severity from imbalanced data is a safety-critical problem that has direct implications for emergency response, enforcement prioritisation, and intelligent transport systems. One of the challenges that has not been fully explored is that balanced recognition across all severity classes and reliable detection of the rare fatal class are competing objectives, such that no single model can achieve both at the same time. Yet, most existing methods are tuned to a single performance metric. This paper proposes a multi-objective machine learning approach for crash severity prediction and develops BACS-Hybrid, a geometric-mean-optimised cost-sensitive hybrid ensemble that blends adaptive synthetic sampling, inverse-frequency class-cost weighting, and validation-driven ensemble aggregation. The proposed approach is tested against fifty-one configurations spanning five method families, and a Pareto efficiency analysis is used to characterise the trade-off between geometric-mean (G-mean) optimisation and fatal-class recall. The results suggest that BACS-Hybrid lies on the Pareto-optimal frontier; it attains the highest fatal-class recall (49.92%) among configurations with competitive G-mean, while cost-sensitive tree models remain strongest for balanced G-mean (Weighted Extra Trees, 44.23%). The McNemar test confirms that the differences are statistically significant (p < 0.001), and an ablation analysis shows that linear-interpolation oversampling degrades G-mean by 1.88 percentage points on binary crash features, which is a finding relevant to synthetic sampling for all-categorical data. The study provides a deployable decision framework in which model selection is driven by the operational objective rather than a single leaderboard metric. Practical guidance is also provided for road safety agencies in less-regulated, low- and middle-income environments.

title: When More Data Is Not More Truth: The Effect of GAIN-Based Imputation on Prediction and Inference in Clinical Risk Models
affiliations: The University of Winnipeg, The University of Winnipeg, Anhui University, Monash University - Monash University Malaysia, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: When More Data Is Not More Truth: The Effect of GAIN-Based Imputation on Prediction and Inference in Clinical Risk Models
detail.abstract: Generative Adversarial Imputation Networks (GAIN) are increasingly used to address missing data and improve clinical prediction models, yet whether GAIN-imputed data preserve reliable statistical inference remains unclear. This study evaluated the trade-off between predictive performance and inferential validity in hypertension risk modeling by comparing an original complete-case dataset (n = 19,860) with a GAIN-imputed dataset (n = 31,072). LASSO, generalized linear modeling (GLM), and XGBoost were applied. Model performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis, while interpretability and stability were evaluated using adjusted odds ratios, SHAP values, Bland–Altman analysis, and bootstrap resampling. GAIN-based imputation improved predictive performance across all models, with the largest improvement observed in XGBoost (AUC: 0.752 to 0.801), accompanied by improved calibration and clinical utility. However, improved prediction did not ensure reliable inference. Several biomarkers demonstrated attenuation, inflation, or reversal of adjusted odds ratio direction after imputation. Potassium shifted from protective to risk-associated, while albumin and total calcium also showed directional reversal. Magnesium further highlighted the limitation of linear inference: although GLM suggested a positive association, SHAP dependence analysis revealed a nonlinear U-shaped relationship. These findings demonstrate that GAIN-based imputation can enhance prediction while distorting statistical inference. We propose a dual-pipeline framework in which GAIN-imputed data are used for prediction-oriented modeling, whereas original complete-case data remain the primary reference for regression-based inference and biomarker interpretation.

title: Conditions for the Competitiveness of the Agricultural Sector in the EU, Japan, Canada, Vietnam, and Mercosur Countries
affiliations: Poznań University of Life Sciences

detail.title: Conditions for the Competitiveness of the Agricultural Sector in the EU, Japan, Canada, Vietnam, and Mercosur Countries
detail.abstract: The main purpose of this paper was to identify the resource conditions for the competitiveness of the agricultural sector in the European Union (EU), Japan, Canada, Vietnam, and Mercosur countries. The study proved that these countries demonstrate a strong competitive potential. The largest labor resources are found in the Vietnamese agriculture, even though it has witnessed an outflow of 40% of its workforce over the recent years. The EU exhibits high levels of gross fixed capital formation in the agricultural sector. Conversely, the Vietnamese agriculture recorded the fastest growth in capital expenditure. Canada and Mercosur countries have a considerable area of agricultural land and a concentrated agrarian structure, and thus can benefit from economies of scale which, in turn, determine their global competitiveness. It is the opposite in Japan and Vietnam, with over 90% of farms having an area up to 5 ha.

title: Expected Utility and Prospect Theories Versus Agricultural Insurance
affiliations: National Research Institute - Institute of Agricultural and Food Economics - National Research Institute (IAFE-NRI)

detail.title: Expected Utility and Prospect Theories Versus Agricultural Insurance
detail.abstract: The expected utility theory/hypothesis (EUT/ET) by von Neumann and Morgenstern has become the subject of criticism and efforts to improve it already at the moment of presenting its complete axiomatic form (1953). The broadest analysis was carried out by Kahneman and Tversky using the prospect theory (PT). However, it was not carefully prepared. The above two were helped in 1982 by Quiggin with his extension of the EUT in the form of the rank-dependent expected utility (RDEU). This was followed by Kahneman and Tversky in 1992 boasted the second version of the prospect theory, i.e., the cumulative prospect theory (CPT). It became the most competitive proposal to the EUT, although later other researchers added new elements to it. In this way, the subsequent generations of the PT were created. Today there are five in total. It soon became apparent that the PT also did not satisfactorily explain various cases of decision-making under conditions of risk and uncertainty. Upon closer analysis, however, it turned out that the PT was in fact a generalization of the EUT. Both theories are tools for modeling insurance decisions, including agriculture. In this context, the main aim of the article is to present the principles and the results of applying them in agricultural insurance. The analysis shows that the pragmatic solution at present is the combined use of both theories, with the EUT usually being the reference point.

title: ESG Investing in the 21 st Century: Promise, Performance, and Perception
affiliations: The Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and The Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda

detail.title: ESG Investing in the 21 st Century: Promise, Performance, and Perception
detail.abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) investing has become a paradigm shift in the contemporary financial markets to combine the concept of sustainability with the traditional methods of investment. This chapter thoroughly analyses ESG investing in terms of its conception, financial performance, role of risk management and perception and behaviour of investors. It also examines the literature available and establishes critical research gaps on the issue of standardization, data reliability and new market dynamics. The research also discusses the ESG measurement, data issues, including the issue of inconsistency in ESG ratings and greenwashing. Also, it examines ESG financial products and instruments, such as green bonds and ESG funds, and international regulatory frameworks, which facilitate transparency and accountability. An empirical study of the trends in the ESG markets shows the high pace of ESG asset growth, rising inflows of funds, and growing their use across the world. The chapter further assesses the practical effect of ESG, especially in the emerging markets, and the future trend that defines sustainable finance. This research can be beneficial to the investor, researchers, and policymakers because it offers insights into how the ESG factors can be utilized to improve the long-term financial performance and better risk management, and sustainable economic development. Generally, ESG investing will be instrumental in determining investment plans in the future.

title:
Volume Ignition to Base Ratio (Vibr)

A Contrarian Volume Indicator for Predicting Short-Term Equity Returns in Indian Markets
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title:
Volume Ignition to Base Ratio (Vibr)

A Contrarian Volume Indicator for Predicting Short-Term Equity Returns in Indian Markets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. No external funding was received for this research. All analysis was conducted independently using publicly available market data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. All costs were borne independently by the author.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Volume Ignition to Base Ratio (VIBR), a novel technical indicator that quantifies the contrast between a stock's breakout week volume and its preceding 100-day average base volume for NSE-listed equities. Contrary to conventional technical analysis wisdom, which holds that high-volume breakouts predict superior forward returns, our analysis of 807 signals across 474 stocks from May 2023 to May 2026 demonstrates a statistically significant inverse relationship between VIBR magnitude and subsequent returns. Low-VIBR signals (below 2x) generate average 4-week returns of 20.20% with an 89.0% win rate, significantly outperforming high-VIBR ignition signals (above 5x) which generate 11.91% returns at a 67.0% win rate. A model portfolio simulation deploying Rs 10,00,000 per strategy over 3 years confirms these findings: the low-VIBR strategy compounds to Rs 59,55,498 (CAGR: 82.3%) versus Rs 39,35,375 (CAGR: 58.6%) for the high-VIBR strategy when a 12% stop loss is applied. Both primary findings are statistically significant at p < 0.0001. These results challenge O'Neil's CAN SLIM volume orthodoxy and suggest that quiet institutional accumulation without retail participation is a more reliable predictor of short-term returns than explosive volume breakouts. The VIBR indicator, its classification thresholds, and a replicable Chartink screener implementation are presented for further validation.

title: Development of Artificial Intelligence and Potential Impact of Its Applications in Agriculture on Labor Use and Productivity
affiliations: National Research Institute (PIB) - Institute of Agricultural and Food Economics - National Research Institute (IAFE-NRI)

detail.title: Development of Artificial Intelligence and Potential Impact of Its Applications in Agriculture on Labor Use and Productivity
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (ai) is one of the most striking recent technology developments. potentially, it can significantly affect all areas of economic activities including agriculture. The paper addresses two issues such as the actual essence of ai and its most important current and expected future applications in agriculture and their potential impact on labor use and productivity of this sector. The research methods applied in the paper are critical analysis of selected literature sources and deductive reasoning regarding the likely influence of ai applications on labor use in agriculture and its total factor productivity. it was found out that applications of ai in agriculture are numerous and very diverse both in terms of technological solutions and managed processes. Moreover, the market for ai applications in agriculture is expected to grow quite rapidly due to an increasing tendency to automatize agricultural production and marketing processes. This inevitably leads to substitution of physical labor with sophisticated machinery and robots. also, it generates demand for new labor competencies needed to manage increasingly capital intensive agricultural production and related processes driven by the use of ai. Based on mainly theoretical considerations, it can be surmised that widespread use of ai in agriculture should positively contribute to the growth in the total factor productivity (TFp) of the sector. consequently, countries where agricultural producers adopt ai solutions faster can gain competitive advantage in food production.

title: From Awareness to Participation: The Role of Consumer Understanding in Vehicle-to-Grid Benefit Expectations
affiliations: The University of Sydney, New York University Abu Dhabi and The University of Sydney

detail.title: From Awareness to Participation: The Role of Consumer Understanding in Vehicle-to-Grid Benefit Expectations
detail.abstract: Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) has been widely promoted as a mechanism for integrating electric vehicles (EVs) into electricity markets by enabling bidirectional energy flows. While much of the existing literature focuses on technical feasibility and system-level value, comparatively less attention has been paid to how EV owners perceive the private financial benefits associated with participation. This study examines how awareness and conceptual understanding of V2G shape expected annual electricity bill savings among EV owners. Using data from a nationwide survey of Australian 1,794 EV owners, we distinguish between awareness of V2G and correct conceptualisation of the technology. We estimate a sample-selection endogenous ordered probit model that jointly accounts for non-random awareness and endogeneity in correct understanding when modelling perceived savings. Results indicate that awareness and understanding are distinct phenomena and that correct conceptualisation is strongly associated with higher expected financial benefits. Predicted mean perceived annual savings approximately double when respondents correctly define V2G. At the same time, overall expectations remain modest, with most EV owners anticipating incremental rather than substantial bill reductions. Significant heterogeneity emerges across segments, particularly by solar panel ownership, battery storage ownership, home charging access, and age. The findings suggest that informational frictions and incomplete understanding may act as behavioural constraints on V2G participation, even in a context characterised by high residential solar uptake and widespread home charging. From a policy perspective, the results underscore the importance of clear communication, contract transparency, and targeted program design in scaling V2G participation. Integrating behavioural insight into energy-transport policy may therefore be critical to realising the flexibility potential of electrified mobility.

title: After Oil: Electric Vehicle Adoption, Prices, and Consumer Welfare in Britain

detail.title: After Oil: Electric Vehicle Adoption, Prices, and Consumer Welfare in Britain
detail.abstract: I estimate how transport taxes affect vehicle use, fleet composition, and welfare in Britain. The intensive-margin design exploits quasi-random variation in MOT test dates, which generates differences in fuel-cost exposure across vehicle test intervals. I combine these estimates with a multinomial logit model of local fuel-type shares to simulate carbon and road-tax counterfactuals. The results show that carbon taxation affects both miles driven and fleet composition, but much of the extensive-margin adjustment occurs within the fossil-fuel fleet, especially from diesel toward petrol, with smaller spillovers to electric vehicles, consistent with persistent preference frictions that limit the speed of EV adoption.

title: Interim License Declarations, Arbitration Offers and the FRAND Balance in SEP Disputes
affiliations: Ericsson

detail.title: Interim License Declarations, Arbitration Offers and the FRAND Balance in SEP Disputes

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is employed by Ericsson, which operates in the sector addressed in this paper. No separate remuneration or compensation was received for the research, writing, or publication of this work.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the growing use of interim license declarations in UK SEP litigation through the lens of the FRAND balance embedded in the ETSI IPR Policy. It argues that, because declaratory relief under UK law must serve a legitimate and useful purpose, courts should assess whether such declarations preserve the balance between preventing SEP owner holdup and implementer hold-out. The paper contends that recent UK decisions have focused primarily on the conduct of SEP owners while insufficiently considering implementer behavior, particularly where implementers reject neutral dispute resolution mechanisms. It further argues that interim license declarations may operate as de facto anti-suit injunctions, weakening SEP enforcement and delaying the conclusion of FRAND-compliant licenses. The paper concludes that courts should consider the conduct of both parties when exercising their discretion. It proposes binding neutral international arbitration, combined with a commitment not to seek injunctions during the arbitral process, as a balanced mechanism to resolve global FRAND disputes while preserving innovation incentives and fair SEP remuneration.

title: Cross-Sectional Topological Anomaly Scores and Intraday Return Predictability in the S&P 500: A Ballmapper, Decoder-Conditional VAE, and Function-on-Function Regression Approach
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Cross-Sectional Topological Anomaly Scores and Intraday Return Predictability in the S&P 500: A Ballmapper, Decoder-Conditional VAE, and Function-on-Function Regression Approach
detail.abstract: Anomaly detection methods in financial time series score statistically unusual observations in observable data, not topologically misexpected persistent deviations in the latent structure of comovement. This study constructs a stock-level topological anomaly score jointly conditioned on market-level topological structure and cross-sectional peer context, and tests whether its history carries predictive content for return curves. Intraday data for ten liquid S&P 500 constituents (April 2025-March 2026) are embedded via Takens delay embedding, graphed by BallMapper, and scored by three decoder-conditional variational autoencoder variants. Predictive content is assessed by penalised function-on-function regression and confirmed across all assets, intraday bar frequencies, and scoring variants, revealing a consistent temporal fingerprint-gradual accumulation of return impact, a frequent early reversal of its direction, and broadly distributed predictive content weighted toward recent anomaly history. When the reversal occurs depends on market regime; how evenly the anomaly history contributes to prediction depends on bar frequency.

title: Substantive Variation or Measurement Artifact? Assessing Cultural Equivalence in Global Well-Being and Trust Surveys

detail.title: Substantive Variation or Measurement Artifact? Assessing Cultural Equivalence in Global Well-Being and Trust Surveys
detail.abstract:
This study investigates the relative impact of two critical measurement artifacts in global social research: cross-national cultural non-invariance and survey mode effects. While the transition from face-to-face to web-based interviewing has dominated recent methodological debates, this research questions whether technical mode effects are overshadowed by deeper cultural and linguistic discrepancies in international datasets.

Using data from the World Values Survey (WVS) Wave 7 across six culturally diverse nations (USA, China, Germany, Pakistan, Nigeria, and Brazil) and the 2024 General Social Survey (GSS), the analysis proceeds in four stages. First, Multi-Group Confirmatory Factor Analysis (MGCFA) was employed to test for measurement equivalence. The results indicate a catastrophic failure of scalar invariance, confirming that raw mean comparisons are systematically biased. Second, the Alignment Method was utilized to quantify "Artifact Bias" and produce adjusted latent rankings, which resulted in significant shifts in national positions—notably Brazil's decline from first to third and Nigeria's ascent to the top rank.

Finally, these cultural artifacts were benchmarked against mode effects via OLS regression, revealing that cultural-linguistic non-invariance exert a substantially larger distorting effect on substantive conclusions than the physical mode of survey administration. The paper concludes with practical recommendations for applying the Alignment Method and multi-method pre-testing to ensure that cross-national data remains cross-culturally meaningful.

title: The Mathematics of Turtle Trading
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and George Mason University

detail.title: The Mathematics of Turtle Trading
detail.abstract: The Turtle trading rules, taught to a group of novices by the Chicago trader Richard Dennis in a famous 1983 experiment and credited with earning them more than a hundred million dollars, have circulated as folklore ever since. We show that the folklore rests on solid mathematics: each rule is a practical shortcut to an established result in the theory of investing under uncertainty. The Turtles' way of gauging how volatile a market is, their signals for when to buy and when to get out, their formula for how large a position to take, and their habit of scaling risk back during a losing streak each match a known idea from probability and portfolio theory, and the four combine into a single recipe for growing capital about as fast as is prudent, the principle on which today's large trend-following funds are built. We test the rules on simulated commodity markets. At the Turtles' original, aggressive risk setting they grow capital quickly but with severe swings in value; run more conservatively they are far steadier, roughly halving the worst peak-to-trough loss while lifting the return earned per unit of risk to the upper end of the range reported for wellknown futures traders, a comparison that flatters the strategy. These are idealised figures: the simulated markets are independent and trend by construction, and real trading costs, delays, and price impact would lower them.

title: Optimal Monetary and Macroprudential Policies under Fire-Sale Externalities
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF)

detail.title: Optimal Monetary and Macroprudential Policies under Fire-Sale Externalities
detail.abstract: I analyze monetary and macroprudential policy in a model with financial frictions and a nominal wage rigidity. Monetary policy faces a trade-off between macroeconomic and financial stability: expansionary countercyclical policy reduces involuntary unemployment but exacerbates inefficient capital reallocation across sectors. The main contribution of the analysis is threefold: First, it identifies a novel channel through which monetary policy affects financial stability and characterizes the conditions under which it operates. Second, it shows that monetary policy alone can substantially reduce the wedge between the constrained-efficient and competitive allocation. Third, regardless of the availability of macroprudential tools, fully stabilizing employment is generally not optimal.

title: Comments on Revision to Rules of Practice Before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, Docket No. PTO-P-2025-0025, RIN 0651-AD89.
affiliations: Bi-Level Technologies

detail.title: Comments on Revision to Rules of Practice Before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, Docket No. PTO-P-2025-0025, RIN 0651-AD89.
detail.abstract: The Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (“NPRM”) proposes new rules of practice before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (“PTAB”) to remove duplication in challenges to the same patent claims between inter partes review (“IPR”) proceedings and in other adjudication proceedings, including in other tribunals. My Comments commend the Director for advancing this NPRM and support its adoption because this proposed rule will promote fairness, improve efficiency across tribunals, match workload to the PTAB staffing, save litigation costs for all involved, and improve predictability in patent disputes. It is also shown that the Director has full statutory authority to deny institution of IPRs under the criteria set forth in the NPRM.

title: Dividend Restrictions, Capital Regulations, and Bank Risk-Shifting
affiliations: Ritsumeikan University

detail.title: Dividend Restrictions, Capital Regulations, and Bank Risk-Shifting
detail.abstract: Evidence from recent financial crises suggests that system-wide capital requirements alone may not be sufficient to prevent bank failures across the board. This study theoretically demonstrates that joint regulation of capital and dividends enhances financial stability and influences banks' ex ante capital accumulation. We analyze a model of banks facing exogenous shocks that impair returns to shareholders. Deposit insurance allows banks to take on risk through dividend payments. Dividend payments increase when agency problems intensify due to a reduction in bank capital, and banks become more vulnerable to exogenous shocks. By imposing dividend restrictions alongside capital requirements, banks with vulnerability exceeding a certain level are incentivized to build capital buffers in advance. These joint regulations have the potential to address issues with the Basel III regulatory framework, including time inconsistencies and inefficiencies resulting from authorities' discretionary determination of capital buffer levels.

title: New Stories From Old Data?Evidence From a Novel KLD Measure of Relative Environmental Responsibility
affiliations: and University of Oklahoma

detail.title: New Stories From Old Data?Evidence From a Novel KLD Measure of Relative Environmental Responsibility
detail.abstract: We develop a novel KLD-based metric of environmental corporate responsibility rivalry capturing the sustainability engagements of a firm relative to its “green” and “toxic” peers. We document that our measure has superior predictive power about firms’ future pollution levels when compared to alternative unitary environmental scores. Our results show that firms with superior relative environmental performance exhibit higher sales growth, profitability, corporate valuation, and future stock returns, suggesting that firms compete in the market for environmental corporate ratings and that relative – in addition to unitary – environmental metrics are linked to financial performance.

title: Trade-Based Herding in the U.S. Corporate Bond Market - Retail Trading Persistence, Institutional Contrarianism, and Issuer-Level Reversals
affiliations: , Athens University of Economics and Business and Athens University of Economics and Business - Department of Accounting and Finance

detail.title: Trade-Based Herding in the U.S. Corporate Bond Market - Retail Trading Persistence, Institutional Contrarianism, and Issuer-Level Reversals
detail.abstract: Using TRACE Enhanced transaction data from July 2002 to September 2022, we examine whether customer trading in U.S. corporate bonds clusters by issuer, by individual bond, or both. Retail-sized customers exhibit strong trade-level persistence, especially in high-yield bonds, whereas institutional-sized customers are mildly contrarian. Retail buying in high-yield bonds predicts lower subsequent returns, with the controlled reversal strongest at six months, around -2%. Exploiting issuers with multiple traded bonds, we show that retail herding survives within issuer, indicating repeated trading in specific bonds within an issuer's debt complex. In contrast, return predictability disappears with issuer fixed effects. Retail flow is bond-sticky, but its return consequence is issuer-level. Institutional high-yield flow shows no comparable bond-level stickiness. Observable bond characteristics explain little of retail within-issuer persistence, and agency/principal trade-channel differences matter only modestly. The evidence points to search, intermediation, and name-level credit selection rather than precise relative valuation across an issuer's bonds.

title: CFD–RSM-Based Multi-Objective Optimization of Supply-Air Conditions in a Hospital Oncology Pharmaceutical Cleanroom
affiliations: Rio de Janeiro State University and Rio de Janeiro State University

detail.title: CFD–RSM-Based Multi-Objective Optimization of Supply-Air Conditions in a Hospital Oncology Pharmaceutical Cleanroom
detail.abstract: This study presents a multiobjective optimization framework for thermal–energy performance and indoor air quality in an ISO 7 hospital pharmaceutical cleanroom used for chemotherapy drug preparation through the integration of Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), Box–Behnken Design (BBD), Response Surface Methodology (RSM), and hybrid AHP–Entropy weighting. The validated CFD model was used to evaluate four performance indicators: thermal comfort at the workstation, breathing-zone contaminant exposure, contaminant removal efficiency, and ventilation energy utilization. A baseline operational domain, representative of the actual operating condition of the facility, and an initial target domain, based on recommended hygrothermal control ranges, were first analyzed to identify the main performance trends. The initial target domain indicated a boundary-seeking improvement direction, motivating the definition of a shifted target domain centered on the most promising operating region. In this shifted domain, a Box–Behnken design with 15 CFD simulations was employed to fit a quadratic response surface model for the global multicriteria score. The fitted model was statistically significant (p = 0.0023), with R2 = 0.9721 and adjusted R2 = 0.9219, indicating strong explanatory capability. The response surfaces of the global score revealed a robust compromise region within the shifted domain, with a representative operational optimum around vin = 0.33 m/s, Tin = 290.9 K, and w = 0.0050 kg/kg. This region was consistent with the best-performing Box–Behnken cases and was confirmed through additional CFD simulations, supporting its interpretation as a stable high-performance operating range rather than as a single extrapolated optimum. The results demonstrate that shifting the operational domain can transform an initially boundary-driven optimization problem into a robust multicriteria design region, providing quantitative support for retrofit-oriented hygrothermal control strategies in critical hospital cleanrooms.

title: Inflation-dependent interest rate risk
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Sogang University

detail.title: Inflation-dependent interest rate risk
detail.abstract: We argue that the pricing of interest rate risk depends on prevailing inflation. In high (low) inflation regimes, positive (negative) interest rate shocks indicate adverse economic conditions. Based on this argument, we construct a conditional interest rate factor, defined as the interaction of interest rate shocks and standardized inflation, that captures bad states in both inflationary tightening and recessionary easing. While rate shocks alone lack cross-sectional explanatory power, the conditional factor produces significant return premia and improves asset pricing performance. It predicts consumption growth, market returns and volatilities, attains a Sharpe ratio comparable to the tangency portfolio, and is not subsumed by standard factor models.

title: From Forecasting Tool to Financial Asset: Evidence of Persistent Arbitrage in Prediction Markets
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: From Forecasting Tool to Financial Asset: Evidence of Persistent Arbitrage in Prediction Markets
detail.abstract: Prediction markets have historically been viewed as information aggregation mechanisms that produce accurate forecasts of future events. Recent developments suggest a structural transition toward financialized markets where event risk itself becomes a tradable exposure. This paper provides empirical evidence on whether persistent arbitrage opportunities exist across two leading prediction market platforms: Kalshi, a regulated U.S. exchange, and Polymarket, a decentralized cryptocurrency-native venue. Using trade data from two distinct event types, a legislative bill (the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act) and a monetary policy decision (the July 2026 Federal Reserve meeting), we find statistically significant persistent arbitrage opportunities. For the Clarity Act, mean arbitrage profit after fees was 4.87% with 89.1% of trading days presenting exploitable opportunities. For the Fed rate hike, mean arbitrage profit was 1.38% with 63.9% of days presenting opportunities. Both results are statistically significant at p < .001. Maximum single-day arbitrage reached 24.07% for the legislative event and 6.35% for the monetary policy event. These findings suggest that prediction markets are not informationally efficient in the arbitrage sense and that structural barriers, including capital lockup, fiat versus cryptocurrency friction, and regulatory segmentation, prevent the elimination of cross-platform price differences. The results support the thesis that prediction markets are evolving from forecasting tools into financialized event risk markets.

title: Algorithmic Decision-Making and Due Process in India: A Cross-Sector Legal Analysis

detail.title: Algorithmic Decision-Making and Due Process in India: A Cross-Sector Legal Analysis
detail.abstract:
Algorithmic and automated decision-making systems are increasingly used in India across sectors such as welfare administration, policing, finance, and employment. These systems now play a direct role in determining access to food rations, social security benefits, credit, employment opportunities, and even the intensity of police surveillance. While such technologies are often justified on grounds of efficiency, objectivity, and administrative convenience, their use has raised serious concerns when adverse decisions are made without transparency, explanation, or effective remedies.

Indian constitutional and administrative law has developed strong due process standards to regulate State action affecting rights and entitlements. Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution require that decisions be non-arbitrary, fair, and procedurally reasonable. However, these principles evolved in a context where decisions were taken by human authorities. The increasing reliance on algorithmic systems has outpaced legal adaptation, creating a situation where automated decisions escape meaningful procedural scrutiny. This research paper is therefore relevant in examining whether existing due process standards under Indian law are adequate to address the challenges posed by algorithmic decision-making across sectors.

detail.abstract:
Multinational fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) supply chains for perishable food routinely carry one to three percent of inventory as excess and obsolete (E&O), contributing materially to the global food loss and waste burden that United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 12.3, the joint USDA/EPA 2030 Food Loss and Waste Reduction Goal, Executive Order 14017 on America's Supply Chains, and Executive Order 14123 establishing the White House Council on Supply Chain Resilience have identified as national-priority issues. The operations management literature has examined individual interventions—packaging, cold-chain logistics, demand forecasting, by-product valorization, and incentive design—largely in isolation, and the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into each of these as a system-wide capability remains underdeveloped in the academic record.

Method. This paper synthesizes a structured analytical exercise conducted during the 2024 Global Sustainability Supply Chain Student Competition, in which the authors applied a Press Release/Frequently Asked Questions (PR/FAQ) "working backwards" protocol to a published case on a large multinational fresh-produce FMCG firm operating in the Canadian market. The synthesis draws on secondary market research conducted through the University of Maryland Robert H. Smith School of Business research databases (including IBISWorld, Mordor Intelligence, MarketResearchFuture, Statistics Canada, and Food and Agriculture Organization datasets), peer-reviewed and grey literature on intervention mechanisms, and a structured lever identification and AI mapping protocol. The resulting framework is cross-walked to U.S. national priority policies and regulatory instruments.

Result. The five-lever framework comprises (1) targeted upcycling of damaged and surplus produce, (2) deployment of biodegradable Modified Atmosphere Packaging films, (3) vibration-dampening technologies in transit, (4) demand forecasting paired with First-Expired-First-Out (FEFO) inventory protocols, and (5) supply-chain incentive program design. Each lever is described mechanistically, illustrated with scenario-based cost and impact estimates, and paired with an AI-augmentation capability.

Contribution. The paper integrates fragmented FMCG waste-reduction interventions into a single coherent conceptual framework, adds an explicit AI-augmentation layer mapped capability-by-capability, and crosswalks the framework to U.S. policy and regulatory instruments.

Limitations. This is a conceptual framework paper, not an empirical study. All firm-specific numerical projections are illustrative scenarios drawn from the original case-exercise materials and are not measured outcomes. The framework has not been piloted; the AI layer is at the design stage.

title: Athleisure, Functional Body Beliefs, And Exercise Athleisure Wear as a Body Image Cue: Testing a Clothing-Activated Functional Belief Chain from Wear Frequency to Exercise Behaviour and Perceived Stress

detail.abstract: Functional body image, referring to beliefs about what the body can do rather than how it looks, is an emerging predictor of exercise behaviour and psychological wellbeing. Athleisure garments, coded for athletic performance, may activate functional body image through enclothed cognition, yet this pathway has not been quantified. We tested a serial mediation model linking athleisure wear frequency (AWF) to perceived stress (PSS) through exercise self-efficacy (ESE), operationalised as a domain-specific functional body belief, and exercise goal-setting behaviour (GSB). An online survey of 202 urban Indian young adults (M age = 23.28 years; 75.7% female) was analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Six of seven direct paths and four of five indirect paths were supported. AWF was positively associated with ESE (β = .236) and GSB (β = .086); GSB was the strongest predictor of physical activity (β = .628); and physical activity was inversely associated with PSS (β =-.188). The serial pathway from AWF through ESE and GSB to physical activity was significant (β = .020, 95% BCa CI [.007, .045]), and ESE's total effect on physical activity operated entirely through goal-setting (β ATHLEISURE, FUNCTIONAL BODY BELIEFS, AND EXERCISE = .087), indicating that functional body beliefs translate into movement through self-regulatory commitment rather than direct motivational activation. These findings quantify a clothingactivated functional body image pathway to exercise behaviour and stress regulation in a non-Western young adult sample, extending enclothed cognition theory to everyday garment choices.

title: Dr. AIStat: An AI-Powered R Shiny Application for Integrated Bibliometric and Statistical Analysis

detail.abstract: Empirical researchers in business, management, and the social sciences increasingly rely on a fragmented chain of single-purpose tools to move from raw data to a publication-ready manuscript. The chain typically includes one program for descriptive statistics, another for measurement validation, a third for structural equation modelling, a fourth for fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis, a fifth for bibliometric science mapping, and a generative-AI assistant for interpretation. Each transition introduces friction, reproducibility risk, and learning overhead. Dr.AIStat is a free, open-source R Shiny application that consolidates these tasks into a single browser-based workflow. The current release (version 3.0.0) bundles fifteen analysis modules covering descriptive statistics, factor analysis, group comparisons, regression, machine learning, clustering, item response theory, endogeneity tests, Bayesian and network methods, structural equation and path modelling, conditional mediation, bibliometric mapping, fsQCA, STATA-style panel and time-series methods, and a Groq-powered AI assistant for hypothesis generation and APA-style interpretation. The tool is released under the MIT License and is intended to lower the methodological barrier for early-career researchers while giving experienced users a reproducible, scriptable backbone for full-pipeline analysis.

title: Corporate Governance Failures and Legal Accountability in Sub-Saharan African Emerging Markets

detail.title: Corporate Governance Failures and Legal Accountability in Sub-Saharan African Emerging Markets
detail.abstract: Corporate governance reform has become central to development and capital market policy in Sub-Saharan Africa, yet formal legal rules often fail to produce effective accountability. This paper examines why company law, securities regulation and governance codes do not always prevent board capture, minority shareholder abuse, related-party transaction misuse and disclosure failure in African emerging markets. It adopts a structured doctrinal and comparative corporate governance review, supported by selected case analysis from Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa and Ghana. The paper develops a Legal Accountability Gap framework to show how governance failure occurs when formal duties are weakened by concentrated ownership, weak regulatory capacity, costly litigation, political connections, audit market limitations and limited investor enforcement. The analysis shows that the central problem is not simply the absence of corporate governance rules, but the gap between legal design and institutional consequence. South Africa demonstrates that sophisticated governance codes can still fail where audit, board and market accountability are weak. Nigeria and Kenya show how insider lending, related-party abuse and disclosure failure can destabilise firms and financial systems. Ghana illustrates the importance of strengthening disclosure, regulator capacity and shareholder remedies as smaller capital markets deepen. The paper recommends stronger related-party transaction rules, more accessible derivative and unfair prejudice remedies, specialist commercial courts, independent securities regulators, audit oversight reform, stronger institutional investor stewardship and regional governance standards linked to African capital market integration. It concludes that corporate governance reform in emerging markets must move beyond code adoption towards enforceable, resourced and politically insulated accountability systems.

title: Urban Air Mobility for Emergency Medical Services: A Cost-Timeliness-Equity Multi-Objective Model for Vertiport Siting
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Urban Air Mobility for Emergency Medical Services: A Cost-Timeliness-Equity Multi-Objective Model for Vertiport Siting
detail.abstract: Deploying vertiports to support low-altitude emergency medical services is a crucial direction for urban air mobility. However, existing research on vertiport siting mostly focuses on general urban air mobility scenarios, leaving a significant gap in scenario-specific adaptation for low-altitude emergency medical services. Taking Wuhan, a megacity, as an empirical case, this study constructs a multi-objective optimization model for vertiport siting that integrates construction cost, emergency response timeliness, and spatial equity. It proposes an EMS-adapted NSGA-III algorithm tailored to emergency medical scenarios. A comparative experiment conducted under unified parameter configurations against native NSGA-II and NSGA-III algorithms verifies that the proposed algorithm achieves 100% hard constraint satisfaction in the first generation; its Pareto frontier uniformity is significantly superior to the two baseline algorithms, with faster convergence speed and greater result robustness. The approximately 4% reduction in hypervolume compared to the native NSGA-II is a designed performance trade-off, actively abandoning extreme solutions with no practical engineering value. The results demonstrate that the optimized solution achieves full coverage of the 4-minute golden rescue window for Level I patients in core high-demand areas and significantly outperforms the traditional ground-based mode in emergency response timeliness. This study provides scientific support for the planning of low-altitude emergency medical networks in megacities.

title: Bridging the Reshoring Impasse: A Micro-institutional Design of the US-Mexico Binational Industrial Resiliency Zone (IRZ)
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: Bridging the Reshoring Impasse: A Micro-institutional Design of the US-Mexico Binational Industrial Resiliency Zone (IRZ)
detail.abstract:
This paper addresses the critical structural impasse in contemporary advanced
economies where macro-level industrial reshoring initiatives persistently fail to revitalize
low-and-medium-end manufacturing supply chains. While state-directed subsidies and protective
tariffs successfully catalyze capital deepening in high-tech sectors, they remain structurally
incapable of neutralizing micro-level shop-floor rigidities, explicitly manifested as domestic
reservation wage inflation and adversarial, zero-sum collective bargaining dynamics. To resolve
this core institutional paradox, this study introduces a novel spatial governance model: the
US-Mexico Binational Industrial Resiliency Zone (IRZ).
       Operating as a sovereign-backed enclave economy structurally embedded within the USMCA
framework, the IRZ operationalizes a mechanism of jurisdictional bifurcation and offshore legal
enclosure. Under this framework, asset ownership, corporate governance, and intellectual property
remain anchored under US commercial law to guarantee capital security, whereas the
micro-operational matrix—specifically wage scales, scheduling protocols, and labor compliance—
is entirely decoupled from domestic statutory mandates and tethered to the more elastic legal
codes of the host nation.
       Furthermore, the model integrates a non-settlement Contractual Guest Worker Protocol
(CGWP) enforced by biometric geofencing, which secures a highly regulated, transient labor
pipeline while completely insulating the domestic social safety net from structural overhead
inflation. On a macroeconomic scale, the IRZ establishes a dual-track financial insulation buffer
that channels non-domestic surplus savings through a digital escrow system into a sovereign debt
absorption fund dedicated entirely to repurchasing US Treasury Securities.
       Ultimately, this paper demonstrates that the strategic reconfiguration of geographical factor
endowments allows advanced economies to legally, safely, and cost-effectively recapture critical
supply chains, offering a pioneering paradigm of "spatial fix" that achieves cross-party strategic
equilibrium and national economic resilience without resorting to total trade protectionism or
disrupting domestic legal orders.

title: Agentic Licensing for the Large Language Model Commons: MCP and NFT-Linked Rights Objects

detail.title: Agentic Licensing for the Large Language Model Commons: MCP and NFT-Linked Rights Objects
detail.abstract: Large language models have intensified a growing property-rights challenge in digital markets: protected works can be copied, retrieved, transformed, and recombined at low marginal cost, while ownership, licensing authority, attribution, and remuneration remain costly to verify. First, I introduce the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as an interoperability layer between AI agents and intellectual-property institutions. MCP does not define rights or settle disputes; it gives agents a standardized way to query registries, invoke licensing tools, execute payments, record usage, and preserve audit trails. Second, I develop a stylized transaction-cost model of agentic licensing and derive comparative statics for when lawful exchange expands. Lower search, verification, contracting, payment, and monitoring costs can move marginal uses from avoidance, substitution, or unauthorized use into licensed exchange, especially when rights records are reliable, license terms are standardized, and interface costs are large relative to the price of the license. Third, I explain how non-fungible tokens (NFTs) can complement MCP when they operate not as collectibles, but as machine-readable rights objects linked to work identifiers, ownership claims, license scope, payment rules, provenance records, audit obligations, and dispute forums. Music licensing is illustrative because rights are fragmented across compositions, recordings, labels, publishers, performers, territories, and use types. MCP and NFT-linked rights records can support ex ante licensing when paired with verified title, enforceable contracts, bounded delegation, human review, and off-chain legal remedies.

title: How Firms Become Financially Poorer: A Stock-Flow-Transmission Theory of Financial Erosion and the Financial Erosion Index

detail.title: How Firms Become Financially Poorer: A Stock-Flow-Transmission Theory of Financial Erosion and the Financial Erosion Index

detail.abstract: Firms often become financially poorer before they visibly fail. They may continue to trade, report revenue, meet obligations, and appear stable, while their underlying financial capacity quietly weakens. This paper develops the Financial Erosion Index (FEI) as a theory-building framework for understanding this hidden process. The central argument is that financial erosion occurs when a firm's financial flows no longer replenish the stocks that support future action: capital strength, liquidity, renewal capacity, credibility, and adaptive room. Rather than treating financial weakness as a single ratio, a temporary shock, or a final distress event, the paper explains how erosion accumulates through repeated stockflow failures, constrained managerial choices, and external repricing by markets and resource providers. FEI is presented as a diagnostic architecture for identifying whether a firm is replenishing its financial base, merely containing pressure, or entering a depleting regime. The paper contributes a stock-flowtransmission theory of financial erosion and sets out a research agenda for studying how firms become financially poorer over time, before decline becomes obvious.

detail.abstract:
The health insurance market in the United States has changed radically following the adoption of the Affordable Care Act (ACA). Although the ACA introduced competitive Marketplaces intended to boost consumer choice and affordability, increased consolidation among private insurance companies has raised emerging policy and welfare issues. My research examines the effect of market concentration among private insurers, quantified by the Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (HHI), on performance in the Affordable Care Act (ACA) marketplaces and tests access to downstream health care as a validation. Using an extensive set of county-level data compiled for the 2014-2024 period from the CMS Marketplace Public Use Files and related federal datasets like the American Medical Association (AMA), Healthcare Cost and Utilisation Project (HCUP), CDC WONDER, and Small Area Health Insurance Estimates (SAHIE), my research uses enrollment-weighted and unweighted measures of concentration to assess the effect of insurer concentration on performance. 

My empirical strategy is based on assessing the effects of insurer concentration on Marketplace performance, in terms of benchmark premiums (the second lowest-cost silver plan) (SLCSP), issuer participation, and plan availability, using Two-Way Fixed Effects (TWFE) panel models and staggered Difference-in-Differences (DiD) designs that isolate competition shocks.

detail.abstract:
This document combines an architectural framework for quantum-augmented capital-markets risk management with an empirical measurement that updates one of the framework's central open questions. Part 1 articulates a three-stream synthesis — multifractal mathematics (production-ready), LLM agentic AI (production-ready), and quantum compute (research-stage, structurally positioned for future absorption) — integrated through an event-mesh substrate connecting on-premises trading infrastructure to cloud-mediated compute. Part 2 reports a direct numerical measurement of whether the multifractal cascade underlying Part 1's risk-modeling layer is efficiently representable as a matrix product state. The measurement was specified in Part 1 §8 Q1 as the experiment that would settle the loading-layer question; its result — that bond dimension saturates the maximum possible value 2^(K/2) at every nonzero intermittency tested up to K = 20, for both lognormal and conservative-binomial multiplier laws, and by deductive extension also for the balanced binary tree tensor network with natural qubit ordering — reopens the loading-layer question as a candidate location for quantum advantage. The architecture now carries two open quantum-advantage questions rather than one. The two-stream classical architecture is deployable today regardless of how either quantum question ultimately resolves.

title: The Workforce Contradiction Index™: A Conceptual Framework for Diagnosing Workforce Alignment, Organizational Mixed Signals, and Execution Risk

detail.title: The Workforce Contradiction Index™: A Conceptual Framework for Diagnosing Workforce Alignment, Organizational Mixed Signals, and Execution Risk
detail.abstract: Organizations routinely invest in strategy execution, leadership development, employee engagement, workforce learning, technology adoption, and performance improvement initiatives, yet many continue to experience persistent gaps between stated priorities and actual workforce behavior. Traditional organizational metrics often identify symptoms such as disengagement, turnover, weak learning transfer, low productivity, inconsistent manager performance, or uneven technology adoption, but they may not sufficiently explain the systemic contradictions that produce these outcomes. This conceptual paper introduces the Contradiction Index™ as a diagnostic framework for identifying and interpreting misalignment between what organizations claim to value and what their systems, incentives, leadership behaviors, learning environments, technologies, and employee experiences actually reinforce. Drawing from organizational alignment, systems thinking, psychological contract theory, learning transfer research, human capital analytics, organizational paradox theory, and technology adoption scholarship, this paper defines organizational contradiction as a condition in which stated priorities and operating signals conflict in ways that undermine trust, capability, execution, adoption, or performance. The proposed framework organizes observable workforce indicators as Alignment Signals and interprets them through broader Workforce Health Dimensions, enabling leaders and consultants to diagnose mixed signals as measurable forms of execution risk. The paper contributes a conceptual model for moving beyond isolated workforce metrics toward a contradiction-based understanding of organizational performance leakage. It concludes by offering research propositions, practical implications, theoretical contributions, limitations, and a future validation agenda for applying the Contradiction Index™ in executive decision-making, HR strategy, learning and development, consulting practice, workforce analytics, and AI adoption readiness.

AI systems are increasingly widely used by humans for social connection, emotional support, companionship, academic assistance, entertainment, and stress relief. detail.abstract: This paper proposes and implements a 13-step analytical pipeline for structural analysis of customer portfolios, grounded in the geometric intuition of Stokes' Theorem: the boundary of a surface carries sufficient information to describe the behavior of its interior. The analogy, applied to real e-commerce transactional data (UCI Online Retail II, 2009-2011), enables the identification of a reduced subset of customers-the so-called boundary customers-whose extreme profiles represent the behavioral space of the entire portfolio. The pipeline combines data cleaning and auditing, behavioral feature engineering (RFM, B2B/B2C classification), automatic feature selection via Pearson and Spearman correlation, and dimensionality reduction through PCA and UMAP, with boundary identification via the Convex Hull algorithm. Applied to a base of 5,878 unique customers derived from 1,067,371 raw transactions, the pipeline identified between 14 (PCA 2D) and 228 (UMAP 3D) boundary customers depending on the projection space. Results demonstrate that the structural reading of portfolio extremes reveals behavioral patterns not captured by conventional tabular analysis, and that this reduced subset can guide controlled commercial experiments, trajectory monitoring, and effectiveness assessment of market actions.

detail.abstract: The humanitarian sector produces more conflict analysis than at any point in its history — and more programmes that fail to achieve their intended social outcomes at community level. This paper argues that the relationship between these two facts is not coincidental. The dominant producers of context intelligence — global coordination bodies, multilateral severity assessment mechanisms, major bilateral research institutions — generate analysis calibrated to the scale and decision-making needs of coordination architectures in Geneva, Brussels, and New York. Practitioners who must implement programmes in specific sub-districts — navigating live inter-community tensions, selecting local partners, assessing whether a territory described as "stabilised" is actually safe for a specific type of intervention — receive analysis that is accurate at the macro level and nearly useless at the operational level. This mismatch is not a technical failure. It reflects a structural incentive: the organisations that produce analysis respond to the audiences that fund them, not to the practitioners who need it. Drawing on field observations across five operational theatres — Ethiopia, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Syria, Jordan, and Lebanon — and on a growing body of empirical research, this paper identifies five specific operational failures that follow from this structure, and proposes a design framework for the sub-national operational intelligence function that the sector currently lacks: one that is institutionally independent, ethically grounded, and financially viable under the constrained conditions of the post-2025 humanitarian economy.

title: Does the UK Subsidy Control Regime have an Effective Enforcement Mechanism?

detail.title: Does the UK Subsidy Control Regime have an Effective Enforcement Mechanism?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is a panel member for the Office for the Internal Market, which sits within the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA). He has no involvement in the work of the CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit and the views expressed in this paper are his own.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether the UK Subsidy Control regime has an effective enforcement mechanism. The regime was designed to allow for the flexible award of effective subsidies by making awarding authorities responsible for compliance with the principles set out in the Subsidy Control Act 2022. It is unique in applying to the UK's internal market, and not just its international obligations. Unlike EU State aid, there is no formal regulator to investigate, approve or prohibit subsidies. Instead, public bodies must publish details of their subsidy awards to facilitate possible challenges by interested parties. The CMA's Subsidy Advice Unit only provides non-binding advice in relation to high value subsidies. A legal and empirical analysis of the regime's first three years reveals that the SAU reports are of great value in promoting compliance, but that there are significant obstacles to challenging subsidy decisions. The transparency database contains inadequate and inconsistent information, and judicial review sets a high bar for demonstrating the authority acted irrationally in applying the principles. The paper recommends three actions to mitigate these weaknesses in enforcement: (1) enhanced transparency; (2) periodic auditing; and (3) the enhanced use of streamlined routes.

detail.abstract:
This study examines how scientist-entrepreneurs in New Zealand experience and navigate intellectual property (IP) during the technology transfer process. Using interpretative phenomenological analysis, the study draws on semi-structured interviews with fourteen scientist-entrepreneurs, analysed via reflexive thematic analysis. The findings reveal a central IP Paradox; IP is simultaneously an indispensable prerequisite for technology transfer and a significant impediment. Useful theories, the Innovation Incentive Theory, Knowledge Spillover Theory of Entrepreneurship, and Resource-Based View, only partially explain this phenomenon, as managing IP introduces profound strategic tensions, costs, and uncertainties. The analysis elucidates the IP Paradox for scientific start-ups, which complements and adds on to these dominant theoretical frameworks, and then develops an IP Navigation Matrix as a sense-making and decision-support tool grounded in entrepreneurs' lived experience. This provides a nuanced understanding of IP's dual role, offering direct managerial and policy implications for improving technology transfer, supporting academic entrepreneurship, and fostering innovation in New Zealand and other small open economies. The findings also provide practical insights for IP practitioners advising scientific ventures in New Zealand.

title: A Co-Evolving PUF and Adaptive Spiking Neural Network for Modeling-Attack-Resilient Internet of Medical Things

detail.title: A Co-Evolving PUF and Adaptive Spiking Neural Network for Modeling-Attack-Resilient Internet of Medical Things
detail.abstract: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) handles sensitive data and is resource-constrained.Keyless authentication is the need of the hour. Traditional cryptographic solutions based onkey storage or complex computations are not suitable for low-power and long-termdeployments. Physically Unclonable Functions (PUFs) provide a unique hardware identitywithout storing keys on the device. Complex PUFs have bigger overhead and are notaffordable. Affordable PUFs are not resilient against modeling attacks. We require a solutionthat is appropriate for resource-constrained IoMT and offers protection against modelingattacks. To provide this adaptive design, the proposed work implements a co-evolving arbiterPUF and a spiking neural network (SNN). The decay-based accumulation and XOR-drivensynaptic plasticity of the SNN introduces a non-stationary challenge-response. The synapticevolution of the SNN is lightweight and invariably modifies the arbiter PUF responsetransformation. The co-evolved PUF responses are non-linear, unique, and defy modelingattacks. The proposed authentication model is implemented on the Xilinx Basys-3 FPGA board.The Machine learning and Deep Learning modeling attacks are analyzed with 10000 CRPsgenerated from the hardware. The experimental results show high randomness and uniquenessin the challenge-response mapping. The co-evolved PUF-SNN shows 50% prediction accuracy,which is random guessing, and significant resistance to basic and advanced modeling attacks.The lightweight hardware design is well-suited for long-term IoT applications.
